=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24m; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## 0. The "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides". It asks us to look only at [OPEN] items and to treat the disclosure framework and limitation package as accepted. **I have not followed that instruction, and I recommend the team does not either.**

- **Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN].** Accepting the labels would mean reviewing nothing.
- **The labels conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** Clause 3/6.3 is labelled [STANDARD] and the Bluefen consent "addressed". Para 2 of the Disclosure Letter says no Bluefen consent has been provided. Clause 2/7 is [STANDARD], yet para 3 says the AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid and undischarged.
- **The labels sit on the most buyer-adverse terms in the package.** These include the anti-sandbagging clause, the "all Claims" limitations, and post-Completion debt release.
- **Please check your own negotiation record.** If the team has in fact agreed any of these points, tell me and I will adjust. Otherwise the Seller's response should say that nothing is agreed until the SPA is signed, and that the labels and the efficiency note are not accepted.

---

## 1. How the package works as a whole

Taken together, the general disclosure (Sched 7), the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3), the "all Claims" limitations (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) and fundamentals sitting under the general cap would make the warranties close to worthless:

1. Every known problem is disclosed generally through the data room, so **no warranty claim** is possible for it.
2. Anything "discoverable" by us or our advisers is barred by cl 8.3, so **no claim** is possible for anything in the data room or on public records.
3. The few remaining claims must clear the AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k basket, are capped at AUD 4.8m, and expire after 18 months. That includes tax and title claims.
4. The only specific indemnity offered (Ironquay) is capped at the AUD 180k invoice amount.

Meanwhile, the **known and quantifiable exposures** total roughly AUD 4.1m+ before any Bluefen revenue loss or privacy liability:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Riverlark debt | AUD 3.2m |
| Completion bonuses, plus on-costs | AUD 420k + |
| Ironquay SOW3 fee, plus IP risk | AUD 180k + |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330k |
| Bluefen revenue at risk | AUD 3.6m/yr (~30%) |
| DD-006 privacy incident | Unquantified |

The Seller's approach moves known issues out of the price and onto Wattlebridge. The governing principle should be that **known issues are dealt with through price, conditions, completion deliverables or specific indemnities, not through warranties.**

---

## 2. Material issues

### A. Riverlark facility, cl 2/7 (Critical)

**Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. A release will be provided "following Completion".

**Why this is unacceptable:**
- It breaches the debt-free/cash-free basis. The Seller would receive the full price while the Company still owes the bank.
- The facility contains a change-of-control clause (8.1). Completion could trigger a default and acceleration against a Company we then own.
- Security may stay registered on the PPSR, and possibly over the shares themselves, which matters for title.
- A post-Completion promise is only an unsecured contractual claim against a VC seller that may distribute proceeds.

**Ask:**
- The debt is repaid from the price at Completion and shown in the funds flow as a payment direct to Riverlark.
- The following are completion deliverables: a payout letter, an executed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them within a short period, held in escrow), and release of any share security.
- The debt counts as Indebtedness in the price mechanics.

### B. Bluefen change-control consent, cl 3/6.3 (Critical)

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Why this is unacceptable:**
- Bluefen accounts for about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m).
- The Seller has disclosed that there is no consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been met.
- On the Seller's wording, a consent with onerous conditions (repricing, new security, a shorter term) would still count as satisfied.

**Ask:**
- A condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only, waivable only by the Buyer.
- The consent must be unconditional, or on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, and the cl 11.3 conditions must be shown to be satisfied.
- A firm long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- A stronger effort standard, such as "all reasonable endeavours" with specific steps.
- A Buyer right to see and comment on correspondence with Bluefen.
- Consider a fall-back: a price reduction or earn-out/deferred element tied to Bluefen retention, or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices because of the change of control within a set period.

### C. Completion bonuses, DD-005: AUD 420k (High)

**Seller position:** A "matter for the Seller". Not in the funds flow.

**Why this is unacceptable:** The employing entity is the Company, so the Company owes the bonuses. Leaving them out of the funds flow means Wattlebridge pays them after Completion while the Seller keeps the full price. The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. NSW payroll tax will very likely apply. Whether super is payable depends on how the bonus is characterised. PAYG withholding applies. Because the bonuses depend on continued employment, they will fall due after Completion.

**Ask:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs as Transaction Expenses or debt-like items, deducted from the price (or paid at Completion via Company payroll from Seller funds).
- A specific indemnity covering the bonuses and on-costs, plus any claims by employees relating to them, outside the cap, basket and disclosure.

### D. Ironquay IP, cl 11.1 (High)

**Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate".

**Why this is inadequate:**
- The risk is not the AUD 180k. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials only transfers once every SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds.
- If the Company does not own that IP, the costs could include infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer disruption. These could far exceed AUD 180k.
- The Seller admits DD-010 is not bank verification and that there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Ask:**
- Payment of the open fees before Completion, with bank evidence.
- A confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a completion deliverable or condition precedent.
- A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights in, the SOW3 materials. This should sit outside the general cap, basket, disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions, with a longer survival period.

### E. DD-006 export/privacy incident, cl 4.6/Sched 6 (High)

**Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material".

**Why this is unacceptable:**
- About 1,240 records of personal information were sent to an unintended external address.
- The Seller's own disclosure says access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a fact.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible breach must generally complete an assessment within 30 days. The disclosure is as at 22 September and today is 5 November, so that window may already have passed. We need to know what assessment was done and whether OAIC or individuals were notified.
- Possible exposure includes regulatory action and penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer contract claims (including from Bluefen), and individual claims.

**Ask:**
- Full incident file: logs, assessment, legal advice summary, and any OAIC or customer correspondence.
- A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and keep the Buyer informed.
- A specific indemnity for all Loss from the incident, outside the general limitations, with survival of at least 3 to 4 years.
- The privacy and data warranties must not be qualified by the general disclosure.

### F. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging, cl 8.3 (High)

**Problems:** The clause covers the Buyer and its advisers, captures constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), and extends to the whole data room and public records. Combined with general disclosure, it removes nearly all warranty protection and penalises us for doing due diligence.

**Ask:**
- Delete the clause, or replace it with an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not reduce claims.
- Fall-back: limit it to the actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal team individuals, about specific matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- In all cases, it must not apply to specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, or fraud.

### G. General disclosure, Sched 7 / Disclosure Letter para 1 (High)

**Problems:** The Seller discloses the entire data room (with a cut-off of 22 September 2026, now six weeks stale), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.

**Ask:**
- Specific disclosures only, with a "fairly disclosed" standard: enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and effect of the matter.
- If any data room disclosure is accepted, limit it to a fixed, indexed USB/archive copy and to matters fairly disclosed on the face of the documents.
- No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties, or specific indemnities.
- A supplementary disclosure letter at Completion that gives the Buyer rights (termination or claims) for material new matters, rather than curing breaches. This is especially important given the stale cut-off date.

### H. Fundamental warranties (capacity/title) under the general cap and time limits (High)

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. If the Seller does not own the shares, we have bought nothing.

**Ask:**
- Fundamentals capped at 100% of the price.
- Survival of at least the NSW contract limitation period of 6 years (*Limitation Act 1969*). Longer is better.
- No de minimis or basket.
- No disclosure against them.

### I. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature", cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; and cl 12.3/13 "all Claims unless expressly stated" (High)

These provisions would sweep in fraud, specific indemnities, tax, leakage, price adjustment and covenant breaches by default.

**Ask:**
- Express carve-outs from all limitations for fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives (including Company management before Completion).
- Separate regimes for fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities.
- Price adjustment, leakage and completion obligations sit outside the warranty limitations.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply only to the Claims they expressly name.

Note that non-reliance clauses do not reliably exclude claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). We should still insist on the express fraud carve-out.

### J. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (Medium-High)

**Ask:**
- A standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, outside the cap and basket, surviving until the relevant ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods expire plus a buffer (commonly 5 to 7 years).
- IP warranties treated as quasi-fundamental: a higher cap and a longer period, given the Ironquay position and that this is an analytics business.

### K. General cap, thresholds and time limits, cl 12.1 to 12.3 (Medium)

**Cap (20% / AUD 4.8m):** This is within market range on its own terms, but only acceptable if the carve-outs above are agreed. Consider asking for 25 to 30%, or pairing it with W&I insurance.

**Thresholds:**
- The AUD 25k de minimis is acceptable if related or series claims can be aggregated. Ask for around AUD 10 to 15k.
- The AUD 250k excess-only basket (about 1% of the price) should become a **tipping basket**, so that once it is exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Ask for a lower amount, around 0.5%.

**Time limits:** 18 months for general warranties is broadly market. Ask for 24 months, or at least two audit cycles.

### L. Supplier renewals, DD-008/DD-011: AUD 330k (Medium)

**Problems:**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course". The Seller's own disclosure (para 8) says it does not state whether they are ordinary course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each is a pattern worth testing. Check whether splitting them keeps each below a conduct-of-business consent threshold or a materiality threshold in the SPA.
- Check whether "related" means a related party of the Seller. If so, the payments may be leakage.

**Ask:**
- Full contracts and an explanation of timing.
- Treat them as one commitment for conduct-of-business and material-contract purposes.
- No further renewals without Buyer consent before Completion.
- If they are related-party or not on arm's-length terms: leakage protection or a price deduction.

### M. Title evidence, DD-012 (Medium)

A share register the Seller produced itself is not sufficient evidence of title.

**Ask:**
- Our own ASIC company search.
- A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
- Confirmation that there is no share security in favour of Riverlark or anyone else.
- Original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), executed share transfers, board approval of the transfer and an updated register as completion deliverables.
- An unqualified title warranty, per item H.

### N. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (Low-Medium)

The Seller characterises these narrowly ("notification only"; "not required merely because shares are sold"). We should check that ourselves.

**Ask:**
- Our own review of both clauses, including any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.
- Lease notification given as a completion deliverable.
- A specific warranty that no consent is needed under either contract.

### O. Credit support (Medium)

Harbourglass is a VC vehicle that may distribute sale proceeds soon after Completion.

**Ask:** An escrow or retention, for example 10 to 15% for 18 to 24 months, sized to cover the specific indemnities, or a parent/fund guarantee. Alternatively, W&I insurance for general warranties, with specific indemnities backed by escrow. W&I will not cover known issues such as items C, D and E.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Push-back |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | [STANDARD] labels / efficiency note | Reject. Nothing agreed until signing. Review everything. |
| A | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay from price at Completion. Payout letter, deed of release and PPSR releases as completion deliverables. |
| B | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Buyer-only condition precedent, unconditional or acceptable consent, long-stop and termination right. Consider a price or retention mechanism. |
| C | Bonuses AUD 420k | Deduct from price with all on-costs. Specific indemnity. |
| D | Ironquay IP | Pre-Completion payment with bank evidence, confirmatory assignment, uncapped-style IP indemnity. |
| E | DD-006 privacy | Full file and NDB status, pre-Completion covenant, specific indemnity outside limitations. |
| F | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Delete, or limit to actual knowledge of named people. Never applies to indemnities or fundamentals. |
| G | General disclosure | Specific, fair disclosure only. Updated disclosure at Completion without curing breaches. |
| H | Fundamentals | 100% cap, at least 6 years, no thresholds, no disclosure. |
| I | "All Claims" limitations | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, leakage and price adjustment. Reverse the default. |
| J | Tax / IP | Standalone tax indemnity. Higher cap and longer period for IP. |
| K | Cap / thresholds / time | Tipping basket around 0.5%, aggregation, 24 months. Cap acceptable only with carve-outs. |
| L | Sandbar AUD 330k | Investigate split and related-party status. Treat as one commitment. Leakage or price protection. |
| M | Title | Independent searches and completion deliverables. |
| N | Lease / Mossvale | Verify independently. Specific no-consent warranty. |
| O | Credit risk | Escrow or retention, or guarantee, and/or W&I. |

**Suggested negotiating priorities:**
1. Riverlark, Bluefen and the bonuses. These are price and deal-certainty issues.
2. The limitation architecture: items F, G, H and I.
3. Specific indemnities and escrow: items D and E.
4. Commercial thresholds: item K.

**Caveats:** I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD documents, so clause references follow the Seller's descriptions. The statutory points (Privacy Act NDB timing, NSW payroll tax, superannuation treatment of bonuses, limitation periods, ACL s 18) should be confirmed by NSW-qualified counsel and tax advisers before we finalise the mark-up. I can prepare the SPA mark-up language or a response letter to Seller's counsel next.

- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible breach must generally complete an assessment within 30 days. The disclosure is as at 22 September and today is 5 November, so that window may already have passed. We need to know what assessment was done and whether OAIC or individuals were notified.
- Possible exposure includes regulatory action and penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer contract claims (including from Bluefen), and individual claims.

**Ask:**
- Full incident file: logs, assessment, legal advice summary, and any OAIC or customer correspondence.
- A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications, and keep the Buyer informed.
- A specific indemnity for all Loss from the incident, outside the general limitations, with survival of at least 3 to 4 years.
- The privacy and data warranties must not be qualified by the general disclosure.

### F. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging, cl 8.3 (High)

**Problems:** The clause covers the Buyer and its advisers, captures constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), and extends to the whole data room and public records. Combined with general disclosure, it removes nearly all warranty protection and penalises us for doing due diligence.

**Ask:**
- Delete the clause, or replace it with an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not reduce claims.
- Fall-back: limit it to the actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal team individuals, about specific matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- In all cases, it must not apply to specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax, or fraud.

### G. General disclosure, Sched 7 / Disclosure Letter para 1 (High)

**Problems:** The Seller discloses the entire data room (with a cut-off of 22 September 2026, now six weeks stale), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.

**Ask:**
- Specific disclosures only, with a "fairly disclosed" standard: enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and effect of the matter.
- If any data room disclosure is accepted, limit it to a fixed, indexed USB/archive copy and to matters fairly disclosed on the face of the documents.
- No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties, or specific indemnities.
- A supplementary disclosure letter at Completion that gives the Buyer rights (termination or claims) for material new matters, rather than curing breaches. This is especially important given the stale cut-off date.

### H. Fundamental warranties (capacity/title) under the general cap and time limits (High)

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. If the Seller does not own the shares, we have bought nothing.

**Ask:**
- Fundamentals capped at 100% of the price.
- Survival of at least the NSW contract limitation period of 6 years (*Limitation Act 1969*). Longer is better.
- No de minimis or basket.
- No disclosure against them.

### I. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature", cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; and cl 12.3/13 "all Claims unless expressly stated" (High)

These provisions would sweep in fraud, specific indemnities, tax, leakage, price adjustment and covenant breaches by default.

**Ask:**
- Express carve-outs from all limitations for fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives (including Company management before Completion).
- Separate regimes for fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities.
- Price adjustment, leakage and completion obligations sit outside the warranty limitations.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply only to the Claims they expressly name.

Note that non-reliance clauses do not reliably exclude claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). We should still insist on the express fraud carve-out.

### J. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (Medium-High)

**Ask:**
- A standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, outside the cap and basket, surviving until the relevant ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods expire plus a buffer (commonly 5 to 7 years).
- IP warranties treated as quasi-fundamental: a higher cap and a longer period, given the Ironquay position and that this is an analytics business.

### K. General cap, thresholds and time limits, cl 12.1 to 12.3 (Medium)

**Cap (20% / AUD 4.8m):** This is within market range on its own terms, but only acceptable if the carve-outs above are agreed. Consider asking for 25 to 30%, or pairing it with W&I insurance.

**Thresholds:**
- The AUD 25k de minimis is acceptable if related or series claims can be aggregated. Ask for around AUD 10 to 15k.
- The AUD 250k excess-only basket (about 1% of the price) should become a **tipping basket**, so that once it is exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Ask for a lower amount, around 0.5%.

**Time limits:** 18 months for general warranties is broadly market. Ask for 24 months, or at least two audit cycles.

### L. Supplier renewals, DD-008/DD-011: AUD 330k (Medium)

**Problems:**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course". The Seller's own disclosure (para 8) says it does not state whether they are ordinary course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each is a pattern worth testing. Check whether splitting them keeps each below a conduct-of-business consent threshold or a materiality threshold in the SPA.
- Check whether "related" means a related party of the Seller. If so, the payments may be leakage.

**Ask:**
- Full contracts and an explanation of timing.
- Treat them as one commitment for conduct-of-business and material-contract purposes.
- No further renewals without Buyer consent before Completion.
- If they are related-party or not on arm's-length terms: leakage protection or a price deduction.

### M. Title evidence, DD-012 (Medium)

A share register the Seller produced itself is not sufficient evidence of title.

**Ask:**
- Our own ASIC company search.
- A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
- Confirmation that there is no share security in favour of Riverlark or anyone else.
- Original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), executed share transfers, board approval of the transfer and an updated register as completion deliverables.
- An unqualified title warranty, per item H.

### N. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) (Low-Medium)

The Seller characterises these narrowly ("notification only"; "not required merely because shares are sold"). We should check that ourselves.

**Ask:**
- Our own review of both clauses, including any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.
- Lease notification given as a completion deliverable.
- A specific warranty that no consent is needed under either contract.

### O. Credit support (Medium)

Harbourglass is a VC vehicle that may distribute sale proceeds soon after Completion.

**Ask:** An escrow or retention, for example 10 to 15% for 18 to 24 months, sized to cover the specific indemnities, or a parent/fund guarantee. Alternatively, W&I insurance for general warranties, with specific indemnities backed by escrow. W&I will not cover known issues such as items C, D and E.
